data.content_ref: inline:SRC_03's corrupted-checklist control is not reliably feasible 'within a single evaluation,' and the target's own counterconditions acknowledge this. The problem explicitly asks for evidence within a single evaluation. The control requires splitting the panel into sub-panels and silently giving one a corrupted checklist. For many tasks with objectively verifiable outcomes, the corruption (shuffled criteria, reversed thresholds) is either detectable by panel members (who may notice internally inconsistent or nonsensical rules), or the split destroys the panel-size/noise-reduction property that the original claim is about, making the sub-panel comparison inapt. The countercondition 'The control is not feasible within a single evaluation' concedes the entire discriminating test can fail to apply. Since the target stakes the ENTIRE ability to distinguish genuine from compliance-driven reliability on this one control ('only if the evaluation includes a corrupted-checklist or shuffled-criteria control'), the infeasibility cases are not edge cases — they collapse the proposal's coverage for the precise problem posed.
